title: [Test fixture] Supervised exercise during chemotherapy: a randomized controlled trial
abstract: In this randomized controlled trial, adults receiving chemotherapy were assigned to supervised aerobic and resistance exercise or to usual care. Supervised exercise during chemotherapy reduced cancer-related fatigue and improved physical function and quality of life compared with usual care. No serious adverse events related to exercise were reported.

title: [Test fixture] Exercise for cancer-related fatigue: a systematic review
abstract: This systematic review found that exercise interventions reduced cancer-related fatigue both during and after cancer treatment. Exercise was safe and well tolerated in most trials. Benefits were also reported for anxiety, depression and quality of life. People with cancer should talk to their care team before starting a new exercise programme, especially if they have low blood counts or bone metastases.
